title: Crossfade KV + Batch Sync — Weekly debrief
content:
Weekly debrief: Crossfade KV + Batch Sync

Date: 2029-03-15 -> 2029-03-18 (captures daily standups Mon/Wed/Fri)
Attendees: Aisha (lead), Ben, Maya, Liam, Carlos, subteam guests: infra-oncall (J. Park), perf-sig (R. Nguyen)

Objective this sprint:
- Continue the crossfade experiment that glues the new fast-path kernel to the adaptive KV-prefetcher and shard-aware batcher.
- Prove stability at 99.9% p50/p95 under mixed short+long sequence workloads (chat + summarization).
- Land initial safety guards for cache-miss amplification and throttle burst coalescing.

High-level summary:
- Crossfade runtime flag (crossfade.v1) is staged on staging and behind rollout gate. We ran 48h soak with synthetic traffic split 60/40 short/long and observed expected improvements for cold-start long sequences: p95 down ~210ms relative to baseline.
- However, we observed intermittent batch growth spikes when prefetch misses coincided with high incoming short-query percent; that led to a few 500ms p95 regressions for short route. Root cause appears to be the batcher waiting for prefetch completion on the fast-path; when prefetch fails it introduces jitter in kernel handoff.
- Mitigation implemented: added a 12ms prefetch timeout and fast forward path that proceeds without KV when timeout triggers. Preliminary eval shows regressions reduced by ~75%.

Key metrics (staging, aggregated, 48h):
- baseline p50/p95 short: 12ms / 48ms
- crossfade p50/p95 short (no-mitigations): 13ms / 120ms (spikes)
- crossfade p50/p95 short (with 12ms timeout): 13ms / 62ms
- baseline p50/p95 long: 230ms / 870ms
- crossfade p50/p95 long: 185ms / 660ms
- throughput (tokens/sec per GPU) long-heavy: +9%
- token cost estimate (microbenchmark): -5% on average for mixed workload assuming 40% reuse cache hit rate

What we tested this week:
- Kernel handshake buffer increase (Ben): bump control-plane handshake window from 8->12 to reduce races when swapping kernels mid-batch. Result: handshake error rate dropped 86% in unit tests, no perf penalty.
- Prefetch timeout (Aisha + Maya): introduced 12ms and 5ms experiments. 12ms chosen for smoother tail.
- Batch split heuristics (Liam): added short-query fast-path that caps coalescing at 6ms for routes labeled real-time. Reduced jitter for short flows.
- Stress soak with infra-oncall (Carlos): replay of production traces for 3x load found a pathological case: when cache eviction coincides with model quantized-kernel warmup, we saw CPU-side scheduling spikes. Filed follow-up ticket.

Blockers and open risks:
- Eviction thundering: edge case where many sessions evict same chunk leads to prefetch storm and temporary memory pressure. Risk level: medium. Owner: Maya.
- Model-variant fallback coupling: routing to a smaller quantized variant currently invalidates prefix cache and causes repeated prefetches. Needs design to reuse compatible KV windows across variant families. Ticket: jira/RW-3402. Owner: Liam.
- Telemetry blind spot: current trace sampling drops some fast-path fallthrough events; need to add a low-overhead counter for prefetch timeouts. Owner: Ben.

Decisions made:
- Default prefetch timeout set to 12ms for crossfade.v1 in canary rollout. Rationale: balances tail for short routes while preserving benefit for long sequences.
- Kernel handshake window increased to 12. Kept as config to revert if thermal issues observed.
- Do NOT auto-escalate to fallback model for first failure; instead mark as transient and allow next token to retry fast-path (reduces variant flip-flopping).

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Maya: implement eviction backoff + write unit tests for evict storm mitigation. Due 2029-03-22.
- Ben: add lightweight prefetch-timeout counter to telemetry + dashboard tile. Due 2029-03-20.
- Liam: prototype cross-variant KV compatibility mapping (design doc) and circulate for review. Due 2029-03-25.
- Carlos: run 72h production trace replay with eviction fix applied; collect tail metrics. Due 2029-03-27.
- Aisha: schedule canary rollout for crossfade.v1 to 5% traffic on Tue (2029-03-19) pending telemetry tile.

Notes for oncall & runbook updates:
- Added entry to runbook: if prefetch-timeout rate > 0.5% and short p95 > 100ms, flip crossfade.v1 -> off for the affected route and notify eng-serving-runtime slack channel.
- Oncall should watch new dashboard tile (ben.crossfade.prefetch.timeouts) and kernel-handshake-error.

Experiment artifacts and pointers:
- perf microbench harness: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/bench/crossfade-micro
- design doc: confluence.redwood/serving-runtime/crossfade-design-doc
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1824 (adds prefetch timeout + fast-forward)

Discussion highlights from Friday sync:
- R. Nguyen (perf) argued for a dynamic timeout that adapts to route RTT. Action: capture per-route RTT percentiles and evaluate dynamic threshold in next sprint.
- Concern about cost regressions under low reuse scenarios — product asked for a mode that disables crossfade for low-cache-hit customers. Action: product/solutions to propose rollout policy.
- Ops requested an escape hatch: ability to set per-customer crossfade override via config-layer. Aisha to scope with product.

Next steps & priorities for next week:
1) Fix eviction thundering and run extended replay (high priority).
2) Ship telemetry tile so canary can be monitored in real-time (high priority).
3) Design cross-variant KV re-use strategy (medium).
4) Evaluate dynamic prefetch timeout in small A/B (low->medium).

Appendix: raw standup snippets
- Mon: "soak looked good except spikes around 03:20 UTC — investigating handshake races" — Ben
- Wed: "12ms timeout seems to knock down the pathological tails; need more replay" — Maya
- Fri: "eviction storm repro'd on 3x trace, scheduling spikes from quant-kernel; Carlos to run bigger soak" — Liam

Questions for leadership:
- Are we comfortable exposing crossfade.v1 to 5% of production (product asks yes pending telemetry)? Please confirm by EOD Mon.
- Should we prioritize the dynamic timeout research over variant compatibility? (engineering preference is compatibility first)

If you want a shorter summary for execs: Crossfade experiment reduces long-sequence tail by ~25-30% and improves token throughput modestly, but introduces a short-route tail when prefetch misses align with batch coalescing. We've implemented a fast timeout mitigation and prepared a cautious canary rollout while we fix a few edge-case eviction and variant-compatibility issues.

-- End of debrief --

Editors: Aisha Khan (lead), Ben Cho (perf), Maya Patel (kv-prefetch), Liam O'Connell (batching), Carlos Ramirez (infra-oncall)
